ABB Ltd Reports Stable Trade Figures Amid Steady Market Demand

ZURICH – ABB Ltd, the Swiss-based leader in electrical equipment, released its latest trade figures this week, reflecting stable performance in both domestic and international markets. The company, which employs more than 5,000 people across Switzerland, continues to maintain its role as a key supplier to the country’s manufacturing and infrastructure sectors.

According to data provided by the Swiss Electrical Industry Association, ABB Ltd’s quarterly exports reached CHF 850 million, showing a marginal increase of 1.2% compared to the same period last year. Imports of electrical components, primarily from European partners, remained steady at CHF 320 million. The figures indicate consistent demand, particularly in automation and energy management systems.

“We are pleased to see sustained interest in ABB Ltd’s solutions, especially from our core markets in Europe and Asia,” said Peter Maurer, a spokesperson for ABB Ltd. “Our ongoing investments in research and innovation are ensuring that Swiss-made technology remains highly competitive.”

Industry analysts noted that the company’s stable performance reflects broader trends within Switzerland’s electrical equipment sector. “There is continued investment in modernization of industry infrastructure, which bodes well for firms like ABB Ltd,” commented Marie Vogel, senior analyst at Helvetic Market Insights. “At the same time, currency stability and strong partnerships with suppliers have helped shield the sector from external shocks.”

Labour representatives at the Swiss Electrical Workers Union welcomed the steady figures. “A stable order book means security for our members,” said union secretary Lukas Frei. “We look forward to continued dialogue with ABB Ltd’s management on workplace improvements and training.”

The Swiss government’s latest economic outlook predicts modest growth in the industrial sector, driven by infrastructure upgrades and ongoing energy transition projects. Local businesses that rely on ABB Ltd’s products, such as the Bern-based rail systems supplier Senn AG, expressed satisfaction with the reliable delivery of components.

With no major disruptions reported, ABB Ltd’s routine trade update underscores the resilience of Switzerland’s electrical equipment industry in a gradually evolving market.
